AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JANUARY 15, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  REVISED
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING - 5:00 P.M.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS
 CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8, Assessor Parcel Numbers 8054-016-901, 8054-016-903, 8054-016-904, 8054-016-905, and
  8054-016-906; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus Gomez, City Manager; Negotiating Party:
  Mercy Housing; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(1) – Los Angeles County Superior Court Case No. 18NWCV00183.

  IV.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(d)(2) –
  significant exposure to litigation in one case.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Reverend Harry A. Matelski
  St. Paul Lutheran Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Eileen Burgos
  Public Safety Cadet

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to recognize the students who painted the holiday window designs at City Hall.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  I.  Neighborhood Enhancement Canvass Results.

  II.  First Responder Christmas video.

  III.  Las Posadas event.

  IV.  Chick-fil-A’s Grand Opening.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of
  December 18, 2018. 825-04
   Report

2.  PAYROLL - Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the periods November 18, 2018 -
  December 1, 2018, in the total amount of $970,240.22 and December 2, 2018 - December 15, 2018, in
  the total amount of $955,812.73. 630

  Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant registers dated
  December 12, 2018 – December 26, 2018, in the total amount of $2,871,933.93, and December 27,
  2018 – January 8, 2019, in the total amount of $984,015.37. 640

  Report

4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Maria Lopez
  and Mireya Morales. 830-12/13

  Report

5.  ORDINANCE NO. 18-1706 – ORDINANCE CREATING A PROGRAM TO REGULATE AND PERMIT
  SIDEWALK VENDING PURSUANT TO CALIFORNIA SENATE BILL 946 – Staff recommends City
  Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 18-1706, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF NORWALK ADDING A NEW CHAPTER TO THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO CREATE A
  NEW SIDEWALK VENDING PROGRAM AND DELETING THE EXISTING BAN ON THE USE OF
  PUSHCARTS OR OTHER NONMOTORIZED VEHICLES IN CONNECTION WITH THE SALE OF
  FOOD OR MERCHANDISE. 612

  Report

6.  PROJECT NO. 7513 – SEWER MANHOLE REPAIR PROJECT – AWARD OF CONTRACTS – Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  award a contract to Sancon Technologies, Inc., in the amount of $43,830 for the Sewer Manhole
  Repair, Project No. 7513;

  b.  award a contract to AKM Consulting, in the amount of $37,035 for construction management
  services; and

  c.  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreements and any amendments, provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in forms approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7513

  Report

7.  PROJECT NO. 7922 - ALONDRA BOULEVARD ACTIVE TRANSPORTATION PLAN (ATP) – AWARD
  OF CONTRACT FOR DESIGN - RESOLUTION NO. 19-02 - BUDGET AMENDMENT - Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 19-02, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2018/19 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO ADD FUNDING TO PROJECT NO. 7922 ALONDRA BOULEVARD ACTIVE
  TRANSPORTATION PLAN (ATP) FROM STUDEBAKER ROAD TO PIONEER BOULEVARD, in
  the amount of $14,000; and

  b.  approve an agreement with Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $12,145
  for environmental documents (CEQA/NEPA), field review forms, and right of way certification for
  the Alondra Boulevard Active Transportation Plan (ATP) from Studebaker Road to Pioneer
  Boulevard, Project No. 7922; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, and
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by
  the City Attorney. 610/1005-04-7992

  Report

8.  TRIENNIAL SHORT RANGE TRANSIT PLAN – FISCAL YEARS 2019-2021 - Staff recommends City
   Council receive and file the Triennial Short Range Transit Plan, and authorize the Director of
  Transportation to submit the updated Short Range Transit Plan to Metro. 1130

  Report

  9.  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION APPROVAL OF BLUE CURB AT 12327 ROSETON AVENUE – No
  action is required unless the City Council elects to review the decision of the Public Safety Commission
  regarding approval of the blue curb. 265

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  10. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200 RESOLUTION

  Report

RESOLUTION

  11. PROJECT NOS. 7359 AND 7364 - LANDSCAPE DESIGN SERVICES – HERMOSILLO AND
  NORWALK PARKS – RESOLUTION NO. 19-01 – BUDGET AMENDMENT- Staff recommends City
  Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 19-01, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2018/19 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO TRANSFER FUNDS FROM PROJECT NO. 7359 HERMOSILLO PARK
  REHABILITATION TO PROJECT NO. 7364 CONCEPT MASTER PLANS FOR NORWALK PARK
  AND HERMOSILLO PARK, in the amount of $62,018; and

  b.  approve an agreement with David Volz Design, in an amount not to exceed $47,018 for Landscape
  Design Services to prepare Concept Master plans for Norwalk Park and Hermosillo Park; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, and amendments provided there is funding
  in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 610/1005-04-
  7359/1005-04-7364

  Report

REPORTS

  12. PROJECT NO. 7849 ACCEPTANCE OF WORK - MEDIAN AND SIDE PANEL TURF REPLACEMENT
  AND DROUGHT TOLERANT PLANT ENVIRONMENTAL ENHANCEMENTS AND MITIGATION
  PROGRAM (EEMP) GRANT ON PIONEER BOULEVARD, IMPERIAL HIGHWAY, NORWALK
  BOULEVARD, AND SAN ANTONIO DRIVE Staff recommends City Council accept the work of PUB
  Construction in the amount of $369,818.95 for the median and side panel turf replacement with drought
  tolerant plant material - EEMP grant project. 1005-04-7849

  Report

  13. PROJECT NO. 7149 ACCEPTANCE OF WORK PIONEER BOULEVARD IMPROVEMENTS FROM
  ROSECRANS AVENUE TO ALONDRA BOULEVARD Staff recommends City Council accept the work
  of Los Angeles Engineering of Covina in the amount of $2,535,730.48 for Project No. 7149, Pioneer
  Boulevard Improvements from Rosecrans Avenue to Alondra Boulevard. 1005-04-7149

  Report

  14. AGREEMENT - RING ALARM SYSTEM – RESOLUTION NO. 19-03 - BUDGET AMENDMENT- Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 19-03, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2018/19 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE FUNDS TO ADD FUNDING FOR THE RING CAMERA REBATE
  PROGRAM, in the amount of $10,000; and
   b.  approve an agreement with Ring LLC for a minimum of $10,000 to provide rebates for the
  purchase of 200 Ring security cameras for Norwalk residents; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 610

  Report

  15. AGREEMENT – PROBATION SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with
  the Los Angeles County Probation Department in the amount of $87,000 to provide a Deputy Probation
  Officer from February 1, 2019 through January 31, 2020; and authorize the City Manager to execute
  the agreement on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 730-05

  Report

  16. VEHICLE ASSET MANAGEMENT POLICY - Staff recommends City Council adopt the Vehicle Asset
  Management Plan as a formal policy for vehicle replacement for City Vehicles.

  Report

  17. NEIGHBORHOOD TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PROGRAM – Receive and file.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated January 10, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
